title: A calendar's own page
question: Each calendar's settings become a tab on its page, as a ministry's do. Which tabs should a calendar have? (2 of 4)

options.label: Events, Regular events, Settings
options.thesis: Regular events becomes a tab of its own; Agenda and Month stay a switch inside Events.
materials: settings cards with Cancel and Save
options.viewport: The calendar's name and a one-line summary with its ⋯ menu (Remove this calendar), the three tabs, then Settings as cards: About this calendar (saves with Save), People on it, Calendar apps and copying.
options.risk: One more tab than the minimum.

options.label: Events and Settings
options.thesis: Only Settings is added; Agenda, Month and Regular events stay as today's switch.
materials: settings cards with Cancel and Save
options.viewport: The same Settings cards; the Events tab keeps the three-way switch beside New event.
options.risk: The switch keeps mixing two ways of seeing dates with a different list (the Pattern map says tabs for different things).

options.label: Events, Regular events, People, Settings
options.thesis: Like a ministry: who is on the calendar gets its own People tab too.
materials: settings cards with Cancel and Save
options.viewport: Four tabs; Settings holds only About this calendar and Calendar apps and copying.
options.risk: A People tab with two or three names on it can feel empty.
